answer: Antibiotics are medicines that kill germs called bacteria, or stop them from multiplying [1][2]. They work because bacteria are built differently from the cells in your body, so the medicine can hit the bacteria and mostly leave you alone. Some antibiotics, like penicillin, break down the tough outer shell of the bacteria so they fall apart [1]. Others stop bacteria from making the building blocks they need to live, or from copying themselves to make more bacteria [1][3]. Antibiotics don't work on viruses, so they won't help with a cold or the flu [2]. If people take them when they don't need them, or don't take them the right way, some bacteria learn to survive them, and then the medicine stops working as well. That's why you should only take antibiotics when a doctor says you need them.
